lenses: fuel sentence, its paragraph and the gate comment
scope: Before the slides of 2008 and 2013, it had raised both fuels by 22 percent or more inside the twelve months my test uses as "before" (Kementerian Energi dan Sumber Daya Mineral, 2014; Menteri Energi dan Sumber Daya Mineral, 2008, 2013).
inventory: 3 items: the one sentence gate scope --since 4 lists, its paragraph, and the shared gate's narrowed comments
method: One lens refuted the three items; a skeptic would re-check any non-confirmed finding, and none was raised. Nothing that determines the post changed after snapshot 5.

findings.claim: Before the slides of 2008 and 2013, it had raised both fuels by 22 percent or more inside the twelve months my test uses as "before" (Kementerian Energi dan Sumber Daya Mineral, 2014; Menteri Energi dan Sumber Daya Mineral, 2008, 2013).
findings.evidence:
lens F (fuel sentence and gate comment): I found no grounds to refute the sentence.

(1) What changed. A diff of draft/.rounds/4.json against 5.json shows one change: line 43, where '2008, 2013 and 2015' became '2008 and 2013'. draft/if-msci-drops-indonesia.md:43 matches the current snapshot, and the site MDX line 72 is identical to it.

(2) Truth, checked with lens/window_check.py, which reads data/fuel_price_changes.csv and results.json:
- The before window is the slide month plus the 11 months before it (household.py:314). Inflation-before is cpi[s]/cpi[s-12] (build_analysis.py:357), and rules.inflation_window_months is 12.
- 2008-10 slide: the window runs 2007-11 to 2008-10. It holds 2008-05-23, Premium 4500 to 6000 (+33.3) and Solar 4300 to 5500 (+27.9).
- 2013-08 slide: the window runs 2012-09 to 2013-08. It holds 2013-06-22, Premium 4500 to 6500 (+44.4) and Solar 4500 to 5500 (+22.2).
- The minimum over the two named slides is 22.2, which prints as '22' at dec0, and 22.2 >= 22. Chart 3 prints '1 rise' under both Oct 2008 and Aug 2013.

(3) Each of the three citations still supports part of the sentence:
- Kementerian ESDM 2014 (sources/fuel/esdm_2014-11-18_siaran_pers_60_SJI_2014.html): 'Pada tahun 2013, harga bensin premium naik menjadi Rp. 6.500/liter (44,4%), sedangkan solar naik menjadi Rp. 5.500/liter (51,1%)'. This covers the 2013 rise, ties RON 88 to 'premium', and gives the 2005 prices of 4.500 and 4.300, which are the old prices for 2008.
- Menteri 2008 (jdih_abstrak_permen_esdm_16_2008.html): 'Bensin Premium : Rp 6.000,00', 'Minyak Solar (Gas Oil) : Rp 5.500,00', in force on the day it was set, 'Ditetapkan ... 23 Mei 2008'.
- Menteri 2013 (permen_esdm_18_2013.pdf, pdftotext lines 87, 89, 161): RON 88 'Rp 6.500,00', Solar 'Rp 5.500,00', 'berlaku pada tanggal 22 Juni 2013'.
- The in-text order (K before M; 2008 before 2013) matches the reference list (draft:138, 140, 144).

(4) An external check I fetched: UNEP (2016), 'Durability as a measure of success' (cbd.int case study, saved at lens/ext_cbd/cbd.txt, lines 423-425 and 472-474). It gives May 2008 as 'gasoline prices from IDR 4,500 to IDR 6,000 and diesel from IDR 4,300 to IDR 5,500', and June 2013 as 'gasoline from IDR 4,500/litre to IDR 6,500/litre and diesel from IDR 4,500/litre to IDR 5,500/litre'.

Notes, none of which changes the verdict:
- The '22' is bound to household.fuel.slowed.min_pct. Its population still includes the 2015 episode (n=3; that episode's minimum is 30.8), so the printed value equals the two-slide minimum only because 2015's is higher.
- The cited 2014 release gives 51,1% for the 2013 Solar rise. 4,500 to 5,500 is 22.2%, so the 51,1 is that source's own error (UNEP and Perpres 15/2012 both give 4,500 as the old price). '22 percent or more' is true under either figure.
- No cited document says the Oct 2005 price of 4,500 / 4,300 still held in May 2008; the manifest row says no stored document lists the 2006 to 2008 changes. UNEP 2016 confirms it did hold.

findings.claim: The fuel paragraph of the prices section in full after round 4 narrowed the slides named in item 1 from 2008, 2013 and 2015 to 2008 and 2013: is each statement true, is each fact cited to an entry whose stored document holds it (including whether each of the three citations in item 1 still supports something that sentence says), and is the paragraph fair read with chart 3 below it?
findings.evidence:
lens F (fuel sentence and gate comment): I read the paragraph (draft.md:43, which matches MDX:72) with chart 3 open.

(a) The Oct 2005 rise:
- Perpres 55/2005 (pdftotext lines 124 and 127) gives Rp 4.500 / 4.300.
- The old prices 2.400 / 2.100 are in Perpres 22/2005 and in Kementerian 2014: 'dari Rp. 2.400/liter menjadi Rp. 4.500/liter (atau kenaikan sekitar 87%) ... solar naik dari Rp. 2.100/liter menjadi Rp. 4.300/liter (atau sekitar 105%)'.
- results.json episodes[2005-08].after has 2005-10-01 at 87.5 / 104.8.

(b) The narrowed sentence: see item 1. All three citations still support it.

(c) The cuts:
- The 2008-10 after window holds 2008-12-01, 2008-12-15 and 2009-01-15. The Menteri 2009 abstract sets Premium and Solar at 'Rp. 4.500,00' from '15 Januari 2009', reviewing Permen 41/2008. Against Menteri 2008's 6,000 / 5,500 that is a cut.
- The 2015-09 after window (2015-10 to 2016-09) holds 2015-10-10, 2016-01-05 and 2016-04-01. Ditjen Migas 2016 (migas_2016-04-01_penetapan_harga.html) has 'Minyak Solar Subsidi 5.650 5.150' and 'Bensin Premium RON 88 Penugasan Luar Jawa-Madura-Bali 6.950 6.450', in force 1 April 2016. So the government cut both fuels.

(d) The Bank Indonesia sentence: the stored page (sources/provenance/ojk-bps/bi_inflasi_definisi.txt) has 'kenaikan harga BBM di tahun 2005 dan 2008, sehingga menyebabkan adanya lonjakan inflasi'. The sentence attributes this to BI, as design 8.7 (design:292-294) requires.

(e) The closing sentence is a disclaimer. The paragraph uses no causal word of the author's own.

Read with chart 3:
- Oct 2008: '1 rise' before, '3 cuts' after.
- Aug 2013: '1 rise' before, 'no change found' after.
- Sep 2015: '3 rises, 2 cuts' before, '3 cuts' after.
The prose now names only the windows where the chart and the text agree without qualification, and leaves 2015's mixed before-window to the chart. The narrowing dropped a case that fit the paragraph's timing pattern (2015 net Premium +12.3%, Solar +25.5%, per r4:item:2), not a counter-case, so it adds no new selection.

One omission predates round 4: the prose does not mention the 2005 before-window rise or the 2004 after-window rise. Round 2 ruled on this (r2:extra:H:3, struck by its skeptic), and chart 3 prints both as '1 rise'.

findings.claim: Two comments narrowed: numbers.py now reads 'One author's several years, (Name, 2007, 2009), are masked only inside a full (...) of the post; in a README or outside parentheses they stay figures.' Is each comment true of the code; do the gate's 246 tests pass?
findings.evidence:
lens F (fuel sentence and gate comment): Tests:
- In place, 'PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s gate/tests -t .' gives 'Ran 246 tests in 14.631s / OK'.
- SHA-256 of all 32 gate files (excluding __pycache__) is identical before and after the run (lens/gate_before.sha and gate_after.sha).

numbers.py:37-38 against the code:
- _CITE_YEARS (numbers.py:40-41) is applied only when readme=False, and only through _CITE_YEARS.finditer(body, p.start(), p.end()) over the spans of _PAREN = r'\([^()]*\)' (numbers.py:39, :82-83). So the several-year mask applies only inside a full innermost paren of the post body.
- READMEs, published fields and extra templates are all scanned with readme=True (numbers.py:142), and chart literals are scanned raw (:139-140). _CITE_SEGMENT (:35-36) cannot match a segment with two or more years.
- lens/probe_comment.py ran 12 cases with 0 mismatches. Masked: post '(Dell, 2007, 2009)', '(Smith, 2001; Dell, 2007, 2009)', nested '(see (Dell, 2007, 2009))', and '(Dell, 2007, 2009, p. 4)'. Flagged: bare 'Dell, 2007, 2009,', '; Jakarta, 2005, 2008;', '; Jakarta, 1850, 1900)', '[Dell, 2007, 2009]', '(Dell, 2007, 2009; see Table (A))', README '(Dell, 2007, 2009)', and a chart literal.

The test comment at test_numbers_pairs.py:159 ('several years are masked only inside a full (...) of the post; anywhere else they stay figures') is true by the same evidence, and its three assertions (:160-162) pass.

Notes:
- The numbers.py comment names the intended APA form, but the regex masks any capitalised, digit-free text followed by two or more years inside a full paren. lens/probe_cite.py shows '(rose by Dell, 2007, 2009)' passing both the numbers and cite checks when Dell 2007 and Dell 2009 entries exist. The comment does not claim the mask is limited to citations, and round 4 recorded this as an accepted widening of existing gaps (r4:item:6).
- In a 'full (...)', 'full' means innermost: a citation paren that contains a nested paren is not masked, and its years are flagged. That errs on the safe side.
